criteria.descriptor: Correctly separates calibration from discrimination, states that AUC depends only on ranking and is invariant to monotonic transforms, accurately describes the reliability diagram and ECE/Brier, and correctly characterizes temperature/Platt/isotonic scaling (including that monotonic maps preserve ranking). No technical errors such as claiming calibration raises AUC or conflating it with accuracy.

Addresses all four asked parts: root cause (calibration vs discrimination + NN overconfidence), diagnosis (reliability diagram + metric on a held-out set), a concrete fix with a named alternative, and what does/does not change (AUC unchanged, threshold re-derivation). Also specifies fitting the calibration map on a separate held-out split.

Justifies the method choice (why temperature scaling suits an overconfident NN, and the isotonic/Platt trade-off) and explains why a monotonic calibration map restores the downstream expected-cost routing while leaving ranking intact, rather than merely listing techniques.
Clear, well-structured explanation using correct terminology (calibration, reliability diagram, ECE/Brier, temperature scaling) with precise cause-and-effect reasoning that a reviewer could act on.

expected_answer_points: Identifies this as a calibration problem distinct from discrimination/ranking, and explains that ROC-AUC is invariant to monotonic score transforms, so high AUC and poor calibration coexist
Notes the systematic over-prediction is consistent with modern neural nets being overconfident, and that the downstream expected-cost use makes correct probabilities (not just ranking) essential
Diagnoses with a reliability diagram (binned mean-predicted vs observed frequency) plus a scalar metric such as ECE and/or Brier score, computed on a held-out set
Fixes with post-hoc calibration fit on a separate held-out calibration split, explicitly not the training data

Names temperature scaling (a single scalar T on the logits) as the appropriate fix for an overconfident NN, and gives at least one alternative (Platt or isotonic) with its trade-off (e.g. isotonic is flexible but overfits small data)
States the fix is a monotonic map, so ranking and ROC-AUC are unchanged; it corrects the probability values, not the ordering
Notes it will not improve discrimination/accuracy, and that the router's decision threshold should be re-derived after calibration
common_pitfalls: Treats the symptom as a discrimination/accuracy problem and proposes retraining, more data, or a new architecture, missing that AUC 0.92 shows ranking is already good and only the probabilities are off
Proposes only lowering the routing threshold; this shifts the operating point but does not make p a valid probability, so the expected-cost math stays wrong
Fits the calibration map (temperature/isotonic/Platt) on the training set, or measures ECE on the same data used to fit it, causing leakage and optimistically good calibration
Claims temperature scaling or isotonic regression will improve AUC or accuracy, not recognizing that monotonic maps preserve ranking and leave AUC unchanged
Confuses post-hoc temperature scaling of logits with the LLM sampling temperature or with 'setting temperature to 0 for determinism', which are unrelated
Offers a single accuracy or AUC number as evidence of calibration instead of a reliability diagram / ECE / Brier score
reference_answer:
This is a calibration failure, not a discrimination failure. ROC-AUC measures only how well the model ranks positives above negatives, and it is invariant to any strictly monotonic transform of the scores, so a model can rank almost perfectly (AUC 0.92) while its numeric probabilities are systematically inflated. Because the router uses p as a literal probability in an expected-cost calculation, miscalibration directly corrupts routing even though the ordering is fine. The consistent over-prediction matches the well-documented tendency of modern neural nets (trained with NLL/softmax) to be overconfident.

Diagnosis: on a held-out split never used for training or tuning, build a reliability diagram - bin the predictions (e.g. 10-15 equal-frequency bins), plot mean predicted probability (x) against observed positive frequency (y) per bin. A calibrated model sits on the diagonal; this one will sit below it. Summarize with Expected Calibration Error (weighted mean of |confidence - accuracy| across bins) and/or the Brier score, and report the bin count since ECE is binning-sensitive.

Fix: fit a post-hoc calibration map on a dedicated held-out calibration set (never the training data, which yields optimistic maps). For an overconfident neural net the standard cheap fix is temperature scaling - learn a single scalar T>1 by minimizing NLL, then divide the logits by T before the sigmoid. Alternatives: Platt scaling (a logistic fit on the scores) or isotonic regression (non-parametric, more flexible but data-hungry and prone to overfit small calibration sets). I would prefer temperature scaling here for its single low-variance parameter, reserving isotonic for when data is plentiful and residual miscalibration remains.

What changes and what does not: all three are monotonic maps, so the ranking and therefore ROC-AUC are unchanged - calibration corrects the probability values, not the ordering, which is exactly what the expected-cost router needs. It will not improve the model's ability to separate urgent from non-urgent (accuracy/AUC stay the same), and the router's dollar threshold should be re-derived afterwards because the score-to-probability mapping has shifted. I would also monitor calibration over time, since drift can re-introduce it.
